description: Searches AgentDrives' tested products by name, domain or what they do. Filters: category, minimum agent level (0-5: 0 Read-only, 1 Needs a person, 2 Gets in, 3 Does the work, 4 Runs on its own, 5 Autonomous), how an agent gets in (access: pay per call, no key, a key by API, its own sign-up…), agent-native payment (proven, or the rails it offers) whether an agent leaves on its own, and surface. Returns the level and its name, how an agent gets in (access) and the five outcomes (find, shown as Learn; access, use, pay, leave: each yes, part (partway: pay part means it reached the checkout but couldn't finish paying; access part, it got in on some drives only), no, unreached (it never got that far) or na), the part scores (holds_up, docs_match: 0-100, null = not measured), where it stopped, the agent-native ways to pay it (pays_with) and whether we made a real payment over one (paid), the bot check that stopped our agent on a way in and its wall_type (network: It judged where our agent connected from and its browser, not a person. Our agent, working on its own from a data center, didn't get through; the owner can let signed agents in. How agents in a person's own browser fare isn't measured yet. challenge: It asks every visitor to prove they are human. Our agent doesn't solve these, and its signature didn't change that: a person does this step, or the owner opens it for agents.), who paid for the drive (origin: editorial, or owner with disclosure "Owner is an AgentDrives customer"), the product's URL (url) and the fields to act on, as find_tools_for_task. Sorted by level, then work done, then minutes to the first call. Up to limit results (default 25, at most 100) from offset; total counts every match, next_offset and more give the rest; with none, try says what next. get_tool gives one product in full by its slug; list_categories gives the category ids. Every field: https://agentdrives.com/openapi.json (ToolSummary).

access.description: only products an agent gets into this way: signup_without_human (our agent signed up and got in without a person, any way), keyless (no key needed), local (runs locally), try_first (try first, claim later), pay_per_call, key_by_api, mcp_signin (our agent signed in to the product's own MCP server, by OAuth, and got in that way), email_signup, browser_signup, by_name (with a GitHub, Google or platform account), person (a person had to set it up: not counted)

agent_can_buy.description: only products an agent paid through an agent-native rail, proven from our side

agent_can_leave.description: only products an agent leaves on its own

category.description: A category id or name from list_categories (e.g. 'crm'); an unknown one is an error that says so

min_level.description: only products at this agent level or higher (0-5)

offset.description: skip this many matches first: the next page starts at the previous answer's next_offset

pays_with.description: only products that take this way to pay: x402 or mpp (agent-native rails, seen or paid) or card (a card checkout); also l402, stripe-projects, acp, ucp, ap2, mcp-payment

query.description: Name, domain or what the tool does, e.g. 'invoicing', 'stripe.com' or 'postgres'; every word must match (the same search as the directory page)

surface.description: only products that offer this way for an agent to work them: api, mcp, cli or sdk

name: search_tools
